note: Calculation: molecular fraction = 1/(1+10^(pH-1.81)). At pH 3.0, fraction = 0.0606, so 20 mg/L free gives ~1.21 mg/L molecular — about 2.4x the stated 0.5 mg/L target (only ~8-10 mg/L free would be needed for 0.5 mg/L molecular). By contrast pH 3.5 (fraction 0.020, 40 mg/L -> 0.8 mg/L) and pH 3.8 (fraction 0.0101, 80 mg/L -> 0.81 mg/L) both check out closely against a 0.8 mg/L target. This matches the known recurring error class of SO2/pH pairs implying the wrong molecular target — here specifically at the low-pH end of the table.
